In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the effect of NE on the fatty acid composition is more pronounced than that of dietary manipulation.

the fatty acid composition in the heart phospholipid fraction was significantly influenced by NE treatment, but the positional distribution of the polyunsaturates in phosphatidylcholine was not altered.
NE treatment and CLO feeding in rats result in a decrease in total phospholipids in rat heart and that the fatty acid composition is changed in a similar way.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the dietary manipulation of fatty acids in rats can be compensated by pharmacological treatment.

NE stress in the rat heart causes a reduction in the total phospholipaids content, which is not due to a change in phospholipid distribution, but rather to a reduction in the amount of phosphatidylcholine.

NE administration in rats, independent of whether the animals were fed with control diet or a fish oil-enriched diet, caused changes in the fatty acid composition in the myocardial phospholipsids and in the positional distribution of fatty acyl residues in phosphatidylcholine and phosphatidyletanolamine molecules, but the changes were less pronounced in CLO-fed rats.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the 2-position in phosphatidylcholine (PC) and phosphatidylethanoline (PE) is the site where the fatty acid exchange is most active.
the fatty acid composition in rat heart phospholipeids can be modified by chronic NE administration and CLO feeding.
the dietary fatty acids are incorporated in phospholipids of the heart, and this incorporation is not altered by chronic NE treatment.
